notes.1a: This question was generally answered well. Many candidates identified within responses factors such as speed, the number of employees the message is going to, whether feedback is required, cost, and the how much/type of information being communicated. Applying the explanation to the dairy business was evident less often. Each explanation needed to be in the context of DD to gain the additional mark for each factor.
notes.1b: Whilst the majority of candidates gave rewardable answers, such as increasing the price or buying cheaper ingredients. Better candidates went beyond this to consider the effectiveness of each of the ways DD could increase added value before justifying their choice in the recommendation. Improving the quality of the product or improving the packaging to enhance the brand image were the most popular ways identified that could lead to an increase in price and the consequences were often a loss of sales. Weaker answers focused on how to increase profit rather than added value.
notes.2a: Many candidates confused the roles of marketing with the four P’s of the marketing mix. Stronger responses did identify marketing roles and recognised that this was a generic question. Weaker responses were written from the point of view of the dairy which often meant the marketing role was not always fully explained even when identified.
notes.2b: The majority of candidates gained marks for making statements about a DD shop increasing costs to set up and run as well as it being 30 miles away from Main City which would restrict the number of new customers. Supermarkets and wholesales were identified as enabling a larger increase in sales however, the price charged by DD would have to be reduced to allow supermarkets to add their own profit margin. Weaker responses where simple statements were made without explaining how the business would be affected could not be awarded above Level 1. Strong responses developed an explanation of how DD’s costs, revenue, sales etc. would be affected by the distribution channel. Stronger responses included a recommendation which fully justified one choice of distribution with comparative comments about why the alternatives were not chosen. Answers were often well applied by recognising the distance of 30 miles from the dairy to the city and the type of products sold by DD.
notes.3a: This question was generally answered well. Most responses were well applied to the business and recognised the products were perishable and could not be stored for very long. The cost of new refrigerators was also given as a reason why storage space was limited.
notes.3b: The majority of candidates gained marks for identifying employees would benefit from lower priced essential products. Many responses mentioned not all employees may consume dairy products making the method ineffective. Profit sharing and job rotation were both well understood. Stronger responses explained the advantages and/or disadvantages in detail to move answers into Level 2. The recommendation was sometimes a repeat of the earlier points made without any consideration of why a chosen method might be more effective than the two methods that were rejected. The job being boring was the most common application in answers but mention of the dairy products or that employees were dissatisfied and left to work for a competitor were also often included as part of the explanation.
notes.4a: This question was generally well answered. Most candidates recognised the interest on bank loans would be lower and therefore more affordable. The second reason was sometimes a repeat of taking out the bank loan to purchase new refrigerators. Better responses went beyond this to give a second reason, for example that customers may increase their purchases of dairy products if they had a higher income from the economy growing. Answers were often applied well by referencing new refrigerators or the dairy products sold by DD.
notes.4b: Candidates need to be reminded to read this question carefully. Marks were gained for comparative statements about the two businesses. However, stronger responses calculated the current and acid test ratios for DD and its competitor. This enabled access to Level 3 when candidates explained the significance of the different liquidity ratios and the difference in revenue. A common misunderstanding in some responses was that profit could be calculated.
